51579222.protein: Inactive tyrosine-protein kinase transmembrane receptor ROR1
51579222.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His-tagged ROR1 frizzled domain (61 to 393 residues) (unknown origin) transfected in baculovirus infected High Five cells assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Binding Kinetics Assays. The binding potency of all final compounds was determined through SPR assays using a GE Biacore X100 instrument (GE, USA), and the protein (ROR1 kinase domain, AA453-783) was obtained from a commercial company (Sino Biological). In brief, the ROR1 protein was immobilized on a biosensor chip (CM5 chip, GE, USA) by amine coupling procedures achieving an RU of 12,500. Then, the chip immobilized ROR1 was activated with sterile buffer (EDC/NHS, 1/1) with a flow rate of 30 μL/min for 7 min and was sealed with ethanolamine for 7 min. The specific interactions of synthetic compounds with the immobilized ROR1 protein were determined. All compounds were dissolved in DMSO and serially diluted with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), and the association of compounds was performed at 25 °C with PBS buffer solution (5% DMSO) with a flow rate of 30 μL/min for 60 s, whereas the dissociation of compounds from the ROR1 was determined for 60 s. The kinetic parameters were provided by the Biacore X100 SPR evaluation software, and the association (ka) and dissociation (kd) rate constants of each compound were used to calculate the equilibrium dissociation constants (KD).
